planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full shade; part of the Dolce series bred for dense mounding habit and vivid foliage color retention through the season.

directions: Dolce Apple Twist Coral Bells forms a dense mound of ruffled, lime-green leaves that twist slightly at the margins, with a silvery overlay that intensifies in cooler weather. Airy sprays of small white flowers appear on thin stems above the foliage in late spring, attracting hummingbirds and small pollinators. Grow in evenly moist, well-drained soil with afternoon shade in hot climates, and remove spent flower stems to keep the mound tidy. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; provide consistent moisture and afternoon shade in hot-summer regions to prevent leaf scorch.

directions: Dolce Cherry Truffles Coral Bells produces glossy, deep burgundy-red foliage in a tight mounding habit, with color that deepens toward near-black in cooler fall temperatures. Small bell-shaped flowers on wiry stems rise above the leaves in early summer, drawing bees and hummingbirds. It performs best in rich, well-drained soil with consistent moisture and benefits from a light mulch over winter in colder zones. Trim old foliage in early spring to make way for fresh new growth.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; a silvery-frosted overlay makes this cultivar especially effective as a shade-garden accent against darker-leaved companions.

directions: Dolce Frosted Berry Coral Bells features ruffled purple-red leaves overlaid with a frosty silver sheen that catches the light in shaded borders, forming a compact, well-branched mound. Delicate white to pale pink flowers appear on slender stalks in late spring, extending the plant's seasonal interest beyond its foliage display. It prefers consistently moist, humus-rich soil and appreciates protection from hot midday sun. Divide every few years to refresh vigor and foliage color intensity.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; part of the ruffled-leaf Dressed Up series bred for an especially frilly, dressed-up leaf texture.

directions: Dressed Up Ball Gown Coral Bells forms a full, rounded mound of heavily ruffled leaves with scalloped edges that give the plant an elegant, layered texture reminiscent of its namesake. Foliage color shifts seasonally, deepening with cooler temperatures, while airy flower stalks rise modestly above the leaves in late spring. Grow in evenly moist, well-drained soil in a shaded border or container, and remove faded leaves as needed to keep the mound neat. This cultivar is valued for its dense, uniform habit in mixed shade plantings.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; part of the oversized-leaf Primo series, this cultivar needs more room than standard coral bells to accommodate its large foliage.

directions: Primo Mahogany Monster Coral Bells produces notably oversized, ruffled leaves in deep mahogany-brown, creating a bold, mounded presence that stands out among finer-textured shade perennials. Its large leaf size and vigorous habit make it a strong anchor plant at the front of a shaded border or in a large container. Grow in consistently moist, well-drained soil, and allow extra spacing compared with standard coral bells cultivars to let the substantial foliage reach full size. Divide every three to four years once the clump becomes crowded.

common_name: Fun and Games Capture the Flag Heucherella

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; part of the Fun and Games series of foamy bells bred for deeply lobed, patterned foliage.

directions: Fun and Games Capture the Flag Foamy Bells displays deeply cut, star-shaped leaves marked with a bold central zone of dark red-brown radiating out to a bright green margin, creating a flag-like pattern. Slender spikes of small white flowers rise above the foliage mound in late spring. It spreads gently by short rhizomes to form a dense, weed-suppressing groundcover in shaded beds. Keep soil consistently moist and amend with compost to maintain the richest foliage contrast.

common_name: Fun and Games Eye Spy Heucherella

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; part of the Fun and Games series of foamy bells bred for deeply lobed, patterned foliage.

directions: Fun and Games Eye Spy Foamy Bells carries lacy, deeply lobed green leaves each marked with a dark maroon central blotch that resembles an eye, fading to lighter edges toward the leaf margin. Delicate white flower spikes emerge above the foliage in late spring, adding fine texture without overwhelming the patterned leaves. The plant spreads slowly by short rhizomes, making it useful as a textured shade groundcover beneath taller perennials. Provide steady moisture and dappled shade for the best leaf markings.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring or early fall in humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil in full to partial shade; part of the Shadowland series of hostas bred for strong color contrast and vigorous habit.

directions: Shadowland Above the Clouds Hosta forms a mounded clump of broad, cupped blue-green leaves with a pale creamy-white center that brightens shaded plantings. Pale lavender flowers rise on tall scapes above the foliage in mid to late summer, though the plant is grown primarily for its striking leaf contrast. It prefers consistently moist, rich soil and thrives in a woodland border or shaded foundation planting. Protect from slugs and snails and divide congested clumps every several years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring or early fall in humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil in full to partial shade; part of the Shadowland series of hostas bred for strong color contrast and vigorous habit.

directions: Shadowland Affair to Remember Hosta produces glossy, deeply veined green leaves edged with a crisp gold margin that widens as the clump matures. Clusters of pale lavender flowers appear on upright scapes in summer above the ruffled foliage mound. It performs best in evenly moist, humus-rich soil with protection from direct afternoon sun, which can fade the gold margin. Divide every three to five years in early spring to maintain a vigorous, well-shaped clump.
